# Sum and difference, one limb

Kernel `add_1_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An approximation $s$ of $a + b$:

$$s \approx a + b.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `a + b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `a += b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `a + b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the limb is converted to `Expansion<T, 1>` first, exactly |
| `a + b` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the limb is converted to `Expansion<T, 1>` first, exactly |
| `add_fast(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `a - b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the sum $a + (-b)$: negating $b$ is exact |
| `a -= b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the sum $a + (-b)$ |
| `a - b` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the sum $a + (-b)$; the limb is converted to `Expansion<T, 1>` first, exactly |
| `a - b` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the sum $a + (-b)$; the limb is converted to `Expansion<T, 1>` first, exactly |
| `finite::add(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the operator itself |
| `finite::add(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `finite::add(a, b)` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `finite::sub(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` | the sum $a + (-b)$ |
| `finite::sub(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `T` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `finite::sub(a, b)` | `T`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |
| `finite::add_fast(a, b)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Expansion<T, 1>` |  |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

The code is one addition of `T`; as for `T`, a compiler that contracts may fuse it with a product it sees ([One limb](../getting-started/guarantees.md#one-limb)).

## Requires

- Every limb of every operand is a finite number of `T`.

## Guarantees

When the requirements hold and no operation of the kernel overflows:

- $s = \mathrm{RN}(a + b)$: the number of the format nearest to $a + b$, ties to even.
- $\lvert s - (a + b)\rvert \le \frac{u}{1 + u}\,\lvert a + b\rvert$.

The constants of the bound, for each limb type, from `gen/claims.json`; `kairn::traits` exports them rounded up to `T`:

| | `double` | `float` |
|---|---|---|
| unit roundoff $u$ | $2^{-53}$ | $2^{-24}$ |
| relative term $c\,u$ | $\frac{1}{2^{53} + 1} \approx 1.1102 \times 10^{-16}$ | $\frac{1}{2^{24} + 1} \approx 5.9605 \times 10^{-8}$ |
| `unit`, `tiny`, as compiled | `0x1p-53`, `0.0` | `0x1p-24f`, `0.0f` |
| `unit_computed`, `tiny_computed` | `0x1p-53`, `0.0` | `0x1p-24f`, `0.0f` |

The compiled constants are the entries `add`, `add_limb`, `add_fast`, `sub`, `sub_limb` of `kairn::traits<T>` (`T` is `float` or `double`; `kairn::traits<Expansion<T, 1>>` is the same): `unit` and `tiny` bound the error relative to the exact result, `unit_computed` and `tiny_computed` relative to the computed one ($\lvert \text{error}\rvert \le \mathtt{unit\_computed}\,\lvert\text{computed}\rvert + \mathtt{tiny\_computed}$).

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the model where no operation overflows. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `add_1_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/OneLimb.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/OneLimb.v), against `add_1_1_spec`, the statement the generator prints from these claims into [`proofs/gen/Statements.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Statements.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions add_1_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/Audit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/Audit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

The statement, as Rocq reads it (the vocabulary, `fmt`, `RN`, `u`, `eta` and `normalized_2`, is defined at the top of the same file; `emin` is the exponent of $\eta$ and `prec` the precision):

```coq
Definition add_1_1_spec : Prop :=
  forall emin prec : Z, (1 <= prec)%Z ->
  forall a b : R,
  fmt emin prec a ->
  fmt emin prec b ->
  let s := add_1_1 emin prec tie_even a b in
  fmt emin prec s /\
  s = RN emin prec (a + b) /\
  Rabs (s - (a + b)) <= (1 / (1 + u prec)) * u prec ^ 1 * Rabs (a + b).
```

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `add_1_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** one rounding to nearest, the bound u/(1+u) of [JR18](../developer/design/phase0/references.md#jr18). **License:** bound: published; proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/add_1_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/add_1_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal models (`proofs/gen/Model.v`, `proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).

```
# One rounded sum. Not a kernel the library calls (its code is a + b): it states the bound of the
# center of a one-limb ball, from which ball_add_1 takes its constant unit_computed. Sharp in the
# form u/(1 + u), and exact in the subnormal range, where the sum of two numbers of the format is
# a number of the format.

s = add(a, b)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 1**: the runs of commit `6f89054` and the supplementary run of commit `f7e0b6d`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone1/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone1/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone1.md#add_1_1)).

## Not claimed

- Anything when an operand is infinite or NaN, or when an operation of the kernel overflows: what is proved and what is not written yet there is in [What holds today](../getting-started/guarantees.md#overflow-and-non-finite-values).
